content: Former spouses sought dissolution of co‑ownership of a flat and garage and the assignment to Partner 1 with a cash equalization. The court confirmed the right to divide at any time and valued the property via a Court‑Appointed Expert. A further issue was set‑off between the equalization due and a liquid, enforceable credit arising from a prior separation ruling. The judge framed the case under community property and residual community rules, addressing whether maintenance‑type claims may offset. Interpretation turned on the nature of credits and art. 1246 c.c. limits on set‑off for maintenance. Principles applied: joint ownership can be dissolved and assets assigned with equalization; liquid and due credits may be set‑off within the lesser of the two, while unilateral offset of maintenance by the debtor is barred. Costs followed the losing party rule and expert costs were charged to the unsuccessful defendant. 1.
